subject: saturated correlates in lavaan vs using auxiliary( ) in semTools

messages.author: 6fb6fd6543d77a99
messages.subject: saturated correlates in lavaan vs using auxiliary( ) in semTools
parts:
Dear all,

I was trying to compare whether the results will be same if i specify a saturated correlates model in lavaan vs using auxiliary( ) from semTools (actually i was comparing which is faster) and found that the results are different. I am not sure if this should be the case. Here are my codes:

library(lavaan)
library(semTools)

# model for generating data
pop.model <- '
f =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3 + 1*x4
f ~~ 1*f
x1 ~~ 0.2*x1
x2 ~~ 0.2*x2
x3 ~~ 0.2*x3
x4 ~~ 0.2*x4

# auxiliary variable is correlated with uniqueness
x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 ~~ 0.5*a
a ~~ 1*a
'

# analysis model for using auxiliary function in semTools
model1 <- '
f =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
'

# analysis model for incorporating auxiliary variables using saturated correlates
model2 <- '
f =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 ~~ a
'

# generate data
set.seed(13243546)

my.df <- simulateData(pop.model, sample.nobs=500)

# 4 missing data patterns with no missing data for auxiliary variables
miss.pat <- list( c(1,1,1,1,1),
                  c(NA,1,1,1,1),
                  c(1,NA,1,1,1),
                  c(1,1,NA,1,1),
                  c(1,1,1,NA,1) )

# create a selection matrix for missing data
selection <- do.call( rbind,
                      sample( miss.pat, size=500, replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.6,
                                                                       0.1,
                                                                       0.1,
                                                                       0.1,
                                                                       0.1) ) )                     

# generate missing data by multiplying data with selection matrix
my.df <- my.df*selection

# using auxiliary( ) from semTools
fit1 <- cfa(model1, my.df, std.lv=TRUE, missing='fiml')
fit.aux <- auxiliary(fit1, aux='a', my.df)

# running saturated correlates model directly
fit2 <- cfa(model2, my.df, std.lv=TRUE, missing='fiml')

Cheers,
Yonghao

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: saturated correlates in lavaan vs using auxiliary( ) in semTools
parts:
Hi Yonghao,

It is quite a pain. You still need to specify the missing argument in the auxiliary function.

fit.aux <- auxiliary(fit1, aux='a', my.df, missing = "fiml")

The code should match. FYI, we will update the semTools to version 0.3-0 in the CRAN in a few days. You can run the auxiliary function from the script directly:

fit.aux2 <- cfa.auxiliary(model1, aux='a', data=my.df, missing='fiml')

You may see the development version from our repository now:

install.packages("semTools", repos="http://rweb.quant.ku.edu/kran", type="source")

I will change the documentation to be clearer. Thank you for your feedback!

Cheers,
Sunthud
